name: Diffusion of an Ink Drop in Water
subject: chemistry
ncert_reference: NCERT textbook portal; Class 9 matter chapter page to verify
educational_goal: Observe diffusion and relate the spreading of particles to temperature and particle motion.
safety_notes: Use warm water that is safe to handle, not boiling water.
Keep liquids away from electrical equipment.

scenes.description: Two identical beakers, one marked warm and one cold, show ink diffusing through water without stirring.

steps.description: Fill one beaker with cold water and one with warm water.
steps.observation: The two beakers contain equal-looking water at different temperatures.
steps.key_visual: The two beakers contain equal-looking water at different temperatures.

scenes.description: Two identical beakers, one marked warm and one cold, show ink diffusing through water without stirring.

steps.description: Place one drop of ink gently in the center of each beaker without stirring.
steps.observation: A dark ink region appears at the point of addition.
steps.key_visual: A dark ink region appears at the point of addition.

steps.description: Observe both beakers for the same time interval.
steps.observation: Ink spreads through warm water faster than through cold water.
steps.key_visual: Ink spreads through warm water faster than through cold water.

scenes.description: Two identical beakers, one marked warm and one cold, show ink diffusing through water without stirring.

steps.description: Record the relative diffusion rates and explain the observation using particle motion.
steps.observation: Higher temperature is associated with faster visible spreading.
steps.key_visual: Higher temperature is associated with faster visible spreading.
